title: Agricultural Extension
source_note: Grounded in standard agricultural extension education curricula (Nigerian ADP model, Rogers' diffusion of innovations theory, and NUC-aligned extension teaching methods) as taught in Nigerian university agriculture programmes.

questions.question: Which of the following best defines agricultural extension?
options: A non-formal, out-of-school educational process that helps farmers improve their farming and living standards through the application of research-based knowledge
A government ministry responsible for issuing farming licenses
A formal university degree programme in crop science
A system of taxing farm produce for rural development
questions.correct_answer: A non-formal, out-of-school educational process that helps farmers improve their farming and living standards through the application of research-based knowledge
questions.explanation: Agricultural extension is a non-formal educational process linking research to farmers to improve productivity and welfare.

questions.question: The Training and Visit (T&V) system of extension was characterized primarily by which feature?
options: Regular, scheduled contact between extension agents and contact farmers on a fixed fortnightly cycle
Extension agents visiting farmers only when invited
Farmers being trained exclusively through radio broadcasts
Extension work being carried out entirely by private companies
questions.correct_answer: Regular, scheduled contact between extension agents and contact farmers on a fixed fortnightly cycle
questions.explanation: The T&V system, adopted widely in Nigeria's ADPs, relied on a fixed schedule of training for agents and visits to contact farmers.

questions.question: In Nigeria, the Agricultural Development Programme (ADP) was primarily established to do what?
options: Deliver integrated extension services and inputs to small-scale farmers at the state level
Regulate the export of cash crops only
Provide university-level agricultural education
Control the price of farm produce in urban markets
questions.correct_answer: Deliver integrated extension services and inputs to small-scale farmers at the state level
questions.explanation: ADPs were established with World Bank support as the main vehicle for delivering unified extension services to farmers in each state.

questions.question: According to Everett Rogers' diffusion of innovations theory, which adopter category is the first to try a new idea?
options: Innovators
Early majority
Late majority
Laggards
questions.correct_answer: Innovators
questions.explanation: Innovators are the venturesome individuals who are the first, willing to take risks, to adopt a new innovation.

questions.question: In Rogers' adopter classification, which group makes up the largest proportion of a typical population, deliberating before adopting after the early majority?
options: Late majority
Innovators
Early adopters
Laggards
questions.correct_answer: Late majority
questions.explanation: The late majority, about 34% of adopters, are skeptical and adopt only after the majority of others have already done so.

questions.question: Which stage of the innovation-adoption process involves a farmer trying out a new practice on a small scale before full adoption?
options: Trial
Awareness
Interest
Evaluation
questions.correct_answer: Trial
questions.explanation: The trial stage is when the farmer experiments with the innovation on a limited scale to judge its usefulness under their own conditions.

questions.question: Which extension teaching method involves working with one farmer at a time, such as a farm and home visit?
options: Individual contact method
Mass method
Group method
Result demonstration method
questions.correct_answer: Individual contact method
questions.explanation: Individual methods (farm visits, office calls, personal letters) involve one-on-one contact between the extension agent and a single farmer.

questions.question: A field day organized to showcase a new crop variety to a large number of farmers at once is an example of which category of extension method?
options: Group method
Individual method
Mass method
Written method
questions.correct_answer: Group method
questions.explanation: Field days bring together a defined group of farmers at a specific location and are classified as group extension teaching methods.

questions.question: Radio and television broadcasts used to disseminate agricultural information to a wide, undefined audience are classified as which extension method?
options: Mass method
Individual method
Group method
Demonstration method
questions.correct_answer: Mass method
questions.explanation: Mass methods reach large, undifferentiated audiences quickly but with less personalized feedback than individual or group methods.

questions.question: What is the main difference between a result demonstration and a method demonstration?
options: A result demonstration shows the outcome of adopting a new practice over time, while a method demonstration shows step-by-step how to perform a specific skill
A result demonstration is conducted indoors while a method demonstration is always conducted outdoors
A result demonstration is for group audiences only, while a method demonstration is for individuals only
There is no difference; the terms are interchangeable
questions.correct_answer: A result demonstration shows the outcome of adopting a new practice over time, while a method demonstration shows step-by-step how to perform a specific skill
questions.explanation: Result demonstrations prove the value of a practice over a season, whereas method demonstrations teach a specific technique or skill.

questions.question: The Farmer Field School (FFS) approach to extension is best described as which of the following?
options: A participatory, season-long learning approach where farmers conduct hands-on field experiments to discover solutions themselves
A one-day lecture delivered by an extension agent in a classroom
A system where farmers are only given written pamphlets
A method restricted to livestock farmers only
questions.correct_answer: A participatory, season-long learning approach where farmers conduct hands-on field experiments to discover solutions themselves
questions.explanation: FFS is a discovery-based, participatory learning approach that runs through a full crop cycle, emphasizing farmer experimentation over top-down instruction.

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT one of the classic elements of the communication process in extension?
options: Taxation
Source
Message
Feedback
questions.correct_answer: Taxation
questions.explanation: The communication process consists of source, message, channel, receiver, and feedback; taxation is not a communication element.

questions.question: 'Noise' in the communication process refers to what?
options: Any interference that distorts or blocks the intended message between source and receiver
The volume of a radio broadcast
The number of farmers attending a field day
The written feedback from a farmer
questions.correct_answer: Any interference that distorts or blocks the intended message between source and receiver
questions.explanation: Noise is any factor, physical or psychological, that interferes with accurate transmission or reception of a message.

questions.question: Which factor is most likely to speed up a farmer's adoption of an innovation, according to Rogers' characteristics of innovations?
options: High relative advantage over the existing practice
High complexity of the innovation
Low compatibility with existing farmer values
Inability to try the innovation on a small scale
questions.correct_answer: High relative advantage over the existing practice
questions.explanation: Relative advantage, the degree to which an innovation is perceived as better than what it replaces, is one of the strongest predictors of adoption rate.

questions.question: Which of the following is a socio-economic factor commonly found to influence a farmer's adoption of agricultural innovations?
options: Farm size and access to credit
The color of the extension agent's uniform
The distance from the farmer's house to the nearest airport
The number of children in the extension agent's family
questions.correct_answer: Farm size and access to credit
questions.explanation: Farm size, income, access to credit, education, and land tenure are established socio-economic determinants of innovation adoption.

questions.question: What is the primary purpose of program planning in agricultural extension?
options: To systematically identify farmers' needs and design activities to address them within available resources
To increase the salary of extension agents
To build new extension office buildings
To replace research institutes
questions.correct_answer: To systematically identify farmers' needs and design activities to address them within available resources
questions.explanation: Extension program planning is a systematic process of situation analysis, problem identification, objective setting, and activity design to meet farmers' needs.

questions.question: In extension program planning, a 'needs assessment' primarily serves what purpose?
options: To identify the gap between farmers' current situation and their desired situation
To determine how many extension agents to dismiss
To fix the price of farm produce
To register new political parties
questions.correct_answer: To identify the gap between farmers' current situation and their desired situation
questions.explanation: Needs assessment identifies problems and gaps that extension programs should address to improve farmers' situations.

questions.question: Which of the following best distinguishes monitoring from evaluation in an extension programme?
options: Monitoring is the continuous tracking of activities during implementation, while evaluation assesses outcomes and impact, often at the end
Monitoring and evaluation mean exactly the same thing
Monitoring is done by farmers only, while evaluation is done by government only
Evaluation happens before a programme starts, while monitoring happens after
questions.correct_answer: Monitoring is the continuous tracking of activities during implementation, while evaluation assesses outcomes and impact, often at the end
questions.explanation: Monitoring tracks ongoing implementation against a plan; evaluation judges the overall effectiveness, efficiency, and impact of a programme.

questions.question: What is a key role of the village or front-line extension agent in the traditional Nigerian ADP structure?
options: Serving as the direct link between contact farmers and the subject matter specialists
Setting national agricultural policy
Approving international trade agreements
Conducting basic scientific research at federal institutes
questions.correct_answer: Serving as the direct link between contact farmers and the subject matter specialists
questions.explanation: Village extension agents work directly with farmers and relay technical problems to subject matter specialists for guidance.

questions.question: A 'subject matter specialist' (SMS) in the ADP extension structure is best described as which of the following?
options: A technically trained officer who provides specialized backstopping support to extension agents in a particular discipline
A farmer who has adopted all recommended practices
The head of the entire ADP
A person responsible only for collecting extension agent salaries
questions.correct_answer: A technically trained officer who provides specialized backstopping support to extension agents in a particular discipline
questions.explanation: SMSs provide technical backstopping in specific disciplines (e.g., crops, livestock, home economics) to extension agents in the field.

questions.question: Which theory suggests that farmers weigh the perceived costs and benefits before deciding to adopt a new practice, similar to a cost-benefit exchange?
options: Social exchange theory
Systems theory
Structural functionalism
Conflict theory
questions.correct_answer: Social exchange theory
questions.explanation: Social exchange theory views human interaction, including adoption decisions, as based on a rational weighing of rewards versus costs.

questions.question: In extension work, 'audio-visual aids' such as posters, charts, and videos are used mainly to achieve what purpose?
options: Enhance understanding and retention of extension messages by appealing to multiple senses
Replace the need for extension agents entirely
Serve as a substitute for farmer field days only
Reduce the cost of fertilizer
questions.correct_answer: Enhance understanding and retention of extension messages by appealing to multiple senses
questions.explanation: Audio-visual aids reinforce spoken or written messages, improving comprehension and recall among learners with varied learning styles.

questions.question: Why is gender consideration important in agricultural extension programming?
options: Because men and women often have different roles, resource access, and needs in farming that extension must address for effective outreach
Because only men are allowed to farm in Nigeria
Because extension messages are legally required to exclude women
Because gender has no bearing on farming activities
questions.correct_answer: Because men and women often have different roles, resource access, and needs in farming that extension must address for effective outreach
questions.explanation: Women play major roles in Nigerian agriculture, especially processing and marketing, yet often have less access to land, credit, and extension services, so gender-responsive extension improves overall effectiveness.

questions.question: E-extension, or the use of ICT in agricultural extension, includes which of the following examples?
options: Sending farming advisory messages to farmers via mobile phone SMS platforms
Only using printed newspapers to reach farmers
Banning the use of radio in rural communities
Requiring farmers to travel to Abuja for every piece of advice
questions.correct_answer: Sending farming advisory messages to farmers via mobile phone SMS platforms
questions.explanation: E-extension leverages mobile phones, internet, and other digital tools to widen the reach and timeliness of extension advice.

questions.question: Which of these is a major advantage of participatory extension approaches over the traditional top-down transfer-of-technology model?
options: They incorporate farmers' indigenous knowledge and local conditions into solution design, improving relevance and adoption
They are always cheaper to implement than any other method
They eliminate the need for any extension staff
They guarantee 100% adoption of every recommended practice
questions.correct_answer: They incorporate farmers' indigenous knowledge and local conditions into solution design, improving relevance and adoption
questions.explanation: Participatory approaches value farmers as co-researchers, making recommendations more context-appropriate and increasing the likelihood of sustained adoption.

questions.question: What is the main criticism of the classical transfer-of-technology (top-down) extension model?
options: It often ignores farmers' local knowledge and specific circumstances, leading to low relevance and adoption of recommendations
It is too participatory and slow
It relies too heavily on farmer field schools
It gives farmers too much control over research agendas
questions.correct_answer: It often ignores farmers' local knowledge and specific circumstances, leading to low relevance and adoption of recommendations
questions.explanation: Critics argue the top-down model assumes researchers know best, often producing recommendations poorly suited to farmers' real conditions.

questions.question: A 'contact farmer' in the T&V extension system serves what function?
options: A progressive farmer who receives direct training from the extension agent and is expected to relay the knowledge to neighboring farmers
The farmer with the largest landholding in the state
A government employee who inspects farms for tax purposes
A farmer banned from receiving extension services
questions.correct_answer: A progressive farmer who receives direct training from the extension agent and is expected to relay the knowledge to neighboring farmers
questions.explanation: Contact farmers act as a multiplier point, spreading knowledge from the extension agent to a wider circle of follower farmers.

questions.question: Which of the following best describes 'relative advantage' as one of Rogers' five characteristics of innovations?
options: The degree to which an innovation is perceived as better than the idea it supersedes
The degree to which an innovation can be tried on a limited basis
The degree to which the results of an innovation are visible to others
The degree to which an innovation is difficult to understand
questions.correct_answer: The degree to which an innovation is perceived as better than the idea it supersedes
questions.explanation: Relative advantage measures perceived superiority of a new idea over the current practice and strongly predicts adoption speed.

questions.question: 'Observability' as a characteristic of innovations refers to what?
options: The degree to which the results of an innovation are visible to other people
How complex an innovation is to understand
How compatible an innovation is with existing values
The cost of adopting the innovation
questions.correct_answer: The degree to which the results of an innovation are visible to other people
questions.explanation: Observability refers to visibility of results; innovations whose benefits are easily seen by others tend to spread faster.

questions.question: What does 'trialability' mean in the context of innovation adoption?
options: The degree to which an innovation may be experimented with on a limited basis before full-scale adoption
The legal process of patenting an innovation
The number of farmers who reject an innovation
The cost of transporting an innovation to the farm
questions.correct_answer: The degree to which an innovation may be experimented with on a limited basis before full-scale adoption
questions.explanation: Innovations that can be tried on a small scale reduce perceived risk and tend to be adopted more readily.

questions.question: Which extension approach emphasizes involving multiple stakeholders (researchers, extension agents, and farmers) working together to develop and test new technologies?
options: Farming Systems Research and Extension (FSR/E)
Compulsory extension
Colonial extension model
Autocratic technology transfer
questions.correct_answer: Farming Systems Research and Extension (FSR/E)
questions.explanation: FSR/E links researchers, extension workers, and farmers collaboratively to develop technologies suited to whole farming systems rather than isolated components.

questions.question: Which of the following is a common barrier to effective agricultural extension delivery in Nigeria?
options: Inadequate funding and poor logistics for extension agents to reach dispersed rural farmers
Too many extension agents relative to the number of farmers
Excessive government investment in extension services
Farmers being too willing to adopt every new technology
questions.correct_answer: Inadequate funding and poor logistics for extension agents to reach dispersed rural farmers
questions.explanation: Chronic underfunding, poor transportation, and low extension agent-to-farmer ratios are widely cited constraints on extension delivery in Nigeria.

questions.question: In evaluating an extension programme, 'impact evaluation' specifically measures what?
options: The long-term changes in farmers' welfare, productivity, or income attributable to the programme
The number of leaflets printed for the programme
The salary paid to the extension director
The number of vehicles owned by the ADP
questions.correct_answer: The long-term changes in farmers' welfare, productivity, or income attributable to the programme
questions.explanation: Impact evaluation looks beyond immediate outputs to assess the lasting effects of an intervention on beneficiaries' lives.

questions.question: Which extension teaching principle states that people learn best when they are actively involved rather than passively receiving information?
options: Principle of learning by doing
Principle of uniformity
Principle of centralization
Principle of secrecy
questions.correct_answer: Principle of learning by doing
questions.explanation: Extension education emphasizes experiential, participatory learning because active involvement improves comprehension and retention over passive listening.

questions.question: What is the main function of a 'field day' as an extension group method?
options: To allow a large number of farmers to see a demonstrated technology or result on-site and ask questions
To register farmers for government subsidies only
To conduct annual audits of extension agents
To hold elections for the local farmers' association
questions.correct_answer: To allow a large number of farmers to see a demonstrated technology or result on-site and ask questions
questions.explanation: Field days showcase results or techniques directly in the field to many farmers simultaneously, encouraging observation-based learning.
